title: Shizuha System Atlas
description: Explore the documented platform from domains to services, internal responsibilities and ordered cross-service journeys. Sources and limitations travel with the graph.

coverage.scope: All 22 service-system-design HLDs in the PLAT-8078 / PLAT-8071 documentation corpus, plus shared infrastructure and named external boundaries.

source_pages.label: HLD: Edge and data-plane system design

supplementary_sources.label: HLD: Cortex Marketplace — Open Provider Onboarding, Quality Verification, Fiat+Crypto Settlement, and Cortex Deployer (CTX-276 family, supply side)

limitations: This catalog describes sourced architecture, not current health, traffic, replica counts, node placement or an exhaustive runtime inventory.
Domains and responsibility-level component boundaries are editorial navigation. A component or process node does not necessarily denote a separate deployment, pod, executable or database.
Shared ID, Cortex, PostgreSQL, Redis and object-storage nodes are canonical references, not duplicated per-service instances. Service ownership and tenant authorization remain separate.

The underlying HLDs contain dated implementation notes. In particular SCLI mixes historical binary/runtime names and explicitly unaudited sidecar rollout; this catalog uses responsibility-level names rather than claiming that topology is deployed everywhere.
The Origin HLD names a database placement disagreement. Its database is intentionally not asserted to be the shared platform database until a canonical source resolves it.
The Edge HLD documents a public relay and shared data path; current DNS, route ownership, host placement and private addresses are intentionally not asserted here.
Ordered flows are representative explanatory journeys, not captured traces, complete failure branches, strict global timing or guarantees about every implementation path.

External provider coverage includes source-named xAI voice and the accepted direct-provider marketplace boundary; proposed relay and settlement details are not presented as deployed facts. This is not a current provider or subscription inventory.
No secrets, credential values, operational controls or instructions to mutate infrastructure are included. Atlas is read-only and never compiles into deployment state.
Updates require source review and a catalog change; no automatic live discovery or source-refresh guarantee is implied.
Books and Inventory HLDs name service-owned records without establishing shared-database placement; the Atlas intentionally omits a physical database link for those services.

Wiki implementation detail is pinned to source revision d16890fb306ef3e95c6ece32a62cfb44c4132eac. Full-page version checking is optional, PageEditor does not submit expected_version at that revision, watch registration does not establish notification delivery, and task definitions do not establish live worker placement.
coverage.summary: 22 service HLDs across eight editorial domains, shared infrastructure and deep Hive/SCLI/Cortex/Wiki responsibilities with six ordered journeys. Wiki internals are pinned to reviewed source; this is architecture evidence, not live operational state.

source_code.scope: Wiki authentication, authorization, versioned writes, attachments, search, collaboration, security events, publication, MCP and browser rendering

flows.label: Agent inference & tool loop
flows.description: Representative documented successful turn. Sequence is explanatory, not a traced request or a guarantee about every engine path.

steps.label: Load the authorized context
steps.description: The runtime consumes the Hive snapshot and restores instructions, tools and session history.

steps.label: Compose the inference request
steps.description: Context and tool schemas are sent directly from the runtime to Cortex.

steps.label: Authenticate the caller
steps.description: Cortex authenticates the documented JWT or API-key caller; Hive is not the request-time proxy.

steps.label: Choose a serving candidate
steps.description: An eligible serving candidate is resolved with the documented affinity preference; routing and capacity may iterate before dispatch.

steps.label: Acquire capacity
steps.description: A successful path obtains admission capacity for the route; no-capacity behavior is policy-dependent.

steps.label: Run model inference
steps.description: The admitted serving engine generates output and streams it through the request path.

steps.label: Execute a tool decision
steps.description: For tool-bearing output the runtime executes the selected tool and obtains an observation.

steps.label: Persist the turn
steps.description: The runtime records session and audit evidence; further observations may drive another inference iteration.

steps.label: Meter the inference request
steps.description: Cortex records tokens, latency and cost; this backend completion can occur alongside runtime tool handling.

steps.label: Release request capacity
steps.description: Capacity is released when request execution finishes; actual cleanup ordering is implementation-specific.

flows.label: Incoming DM → agent reply
flows.description: An authorized owner message can wake a hibernated seat; message admission is not an unconditional reply obligation.

steps.label: Persist the message
steps.description: Connect authenticates and persists the conversation message before delivery.

steps.label: Admit the owner wake
steps.description: Connect requests a wake for the real owner DM through the Hive lifecycle boundary.

steps.label: Converge runtime state
steps.description: Hive requests the appropriate workload state; an already-running seat need not restart.

steps.label: Make the runtime available
steps.description: The desired runtime is made available under Hive-owned configuration.

steps.label: Deliver the admitted message
steps.description: Connect delivers the inbox message to the reachable runtime.

steps.label: Arbitrate against assigned work
steps.description: The runtime considers the DM alongside authorized alerts and assigned tasks.

steps.label: Choose explicit delivery
steps.description: A reply is a deliberate tool action, not automatic publication of private turn text.

steps.label: Publish the reply
steps.description: The delivery tool sends the authorized response through Connect.

flows.label: Reviewed change → deployed artifact
flows.description: Canonical Origin/CI delivery path from a reviewed change to verified workload rollout; no automatic reverse-compilation from Atlas.

steps.label: Submit the canonical change
steps.description: The author submits the exact source change to the canonical repository and review surface.

steps.label: Run isolated presubmit
steps.description: The broker tests the advertised head and base in credential-free jobs.

steps.label: Admit the reviewed merge
steps.description: The merge gate checks the exact candidate, current generation and required verdict.

steps.label: Advance canonical source
steps.description: Only the admitted reviewed change advances the canonical deployment source.

steps.label: Dispatch deployment CI
steps.description: The canonical source event selects the deployment workflow.

steps.label: Run the build/deploy job
steps.description: The scheduler hands the exact workflow to the runner.

steps.label: Publish the image artifact
steps.description: CI publishes the documented multi-architecture artifact.

steps.label: Roll and verify
steps.description: The runner applies the desired workload and verifies exact observed generation and availability.

steps.label: Record deployment evidence
steps.description: Deployment outcome is correlated to the source SHA; merge success alone is not deployment proof.

flows.label: Login → scoped product access
flows.description: Representative human login and local product verification path. Mint-time membership composition is distinct from per-request authorization.

steps.label: Start interactive login
steps.description: The human enters the platform login flow before returning to the requested product.

steps.label: Authenticate and establish a session
steps.description: ID authenticates and records the session before issuing tokens.

steps.label: Resolve membership projection
steps.description: The mint path obtains signed, subject-bound organization/project membership evidence.

steps.label: Read authorized roster evidence
steps.description: Admin composes Pulse roster evidence with its local organization membership records.

steps.label: Return the composed projection
steps.description: Projection failure is typed and fail-closed, not authoritative empty claims.

steps.label: Return the signed session
steps.description: The browser receives the platform session and returns to the product.

steps.label: Call the product as the caller
steps.description: The request carries the caller identity; the BFF cannot widen organization scope.

steps.label: Discover verification keys
steps.description: The verifier obtains or reuses cached public keys and verifies the token locally before product authorization.

steps.label: Apply downstream authorization
steps.description: The downstream service receives the caller identity and independently reapplies its own authorization.

flows.label: Wiki: authorized read to Mermaid viewer
flows.description: A representative signed-in page read: route resolution, identity and visibility checks, serialized content, sanitized rendering and optional diagram viewing. Anonymous reads take a public-only branch; sequence edges are logical stages, not separate network services.

steps.label: Resolve the page route
steps.description: The space/slug reader lists matching pages then retrieves the selected UUID through the shared REST client.

steps.label: Verify the bearer token
steps.description: The backend validates the authenticated request and revocation state.

steps.label: Build the caller's organization context
steps.description: Resolve memberships from the signed token, with the explicit legacy missing-claim fallback.

steps.label: Enforce organization and space visibility
steps.description: A requested org cannot create a grant; filter accessible pages using visibility, ownership and membership.

steps.label: Retrieve the authorized page
steps.description: The ViewSet resolves the filtered object and prepares its detail response.

steps.label: Render the returned representation
steps.description: The browser receives content_text, content_json and version, chooses the applicable representation and sanitizes its HTML.

steps.label: Hydrate Mermaid fences
steps.description: Escaped diagram source placeholders become Mermaid-generated SVG under strict-security configuration.

steps.label: Optionally inspect the diagram
steps.description: Only if the reader chooses the affordance, open the interactive SVG viewer.

flows.label: Wiki: version-guarded MCP page edit
flows.description: A representative full-page MCP update where the caller supplies expected_version. The guarded path rejects stale edits and persists changed page/version records transactionally; omission of expected_version is explicitly not CAS-protected, and section edits use a separate hash-guarded path.

steps.label: Translate Markdown into both page fields
steps.description: The MCP tool preserves Markdown content_text and derives TipTap content_json, adding the caller's expected_version.

steps.label: Choose effective request identity
steps.description: Build caller or explicit delegation headers and optional organization scope.

steps.label: Send the page update to REST
steps.description: MCP sends PATCH to the normal page endpoint rather than bypassing backend authorization.

steps.label: Authenticate the update
steps.description: JWT signature and revocation checks establish the caller.

steps.label: Resolve caller memberships
steps.description: Build the request's membership context before object and action permissions.

steps.label: Authorize the mutation
steps.description: Resolve the page within its visibility boundary and apply the resource's write permission rules.

steps.label: Lock authoritative page state
steps.description: The full-page writer opens a transaction and locks the page and relevant parent rows.

steps.label: Check version and content guards
steps.description: Compare the supplied expected_version, reject unknown fields and unconfirmed dramatic shrink, and return unchanged for a no-op.

steps.label: Save changed page and revision
steps.description: Increment the page version and create its PageVersion snapshot in the same transaction; page-save indexing is a signal side effect.

steps.label: Synchronize the full-page link index
steps.description: Resolve references and collect link warnings before the successful update completes.
